title: #mexodus #hiphopmusical #livelooping #theatrereview #theatretok
transcript: The other night, I caught the first preview of Mexodus at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre. This is a live-looped hip hop musical by Brian Quijada and Nygel D. Robinson about the Underground Railroad to Mexico. Thanks to this piece, I've learned that thousands of enslaved people escaped from the United States by crossing the southern border into Mexico in the 1800s. This musical is historical fiction and tells a version of what that may have looked like. Musically, I was super impressed — the live looping is really cool and leverages over a dozen instruments, as well as everyday objects that function as instruments. It draws a lot of influence from hip hop, but also contemporary R&B, musical theater, Mexican folklore, and Black spirituals. Lyrically, I thought it was a little hit or miss, though my frame of reference for lyricism in hip hop musicals is Hamilton, which sets kind of an unfairly high bar. Overall though, I thought this was a really cool piece, it's unlike anything else on a major stage in New York right now. And for a first preview, it went off without a hitch, which for a show with such precise cues and musicality, was especially impressive Brian and Nygel have managed to make a remarkably original, educational, and richly layered piece. If you're interested, it's running downtown through October 18th. With that, another program for my collection.
